newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's Bucaram concedes he has lost power.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Bucaram concedes he has lost power.

text.p: Ecuador's Abdala Bucaram conceded on Sunday that he had been stripped of his presidential powers in what he described as a "congressional coup" that was backed by the country's armed forces.

Bucaram's statement, in a live interview with national television at about 2:15 a.m. (0715 GMT), marked his first concession of defeat since Congress voted him out of office three days ago on grounds of mental incompentency.

"Ecuador is going to be a disaster and I can assure that the people will ask me to return within a month and a half," Bucaram said in the interview from his home in the Pacific coast city of Guayaquil.

"This is something unheard of in history," he added, referring to a reported agreement between lawmakers and powerful military leaders clearing the way for Vice President Rosalia Arteaga to be sworn in as interim president.
"This is the dictatorhsip of the national Congress," he added, saying that while he remained the country's duly elected president he had effectively been stripped of all possibility to rule.

Bucaram called his summary ouster by Congress a gross injustice, accused the military of having "intervened politically" in national affairs, and said the "congressional coup" was certain to shake international confidence in Ecuador's democratic institutions.
